items.t: 모플랫, 충남에서 차량용 차세대 ‘QD-LED 라이팅’ 개발 본격화
items.d: ‘자발광 퀀텀닷 LED(Quantum Dot LED, 양자점 발광 소재)’ 기술을 자동차 라이팅 및 디스플레이 분야에 접목하고 있는 스타트업 ‘모플랫’이 충남 천안에서 본격적인 공정 기술 확보에 나선다.20일 모플랫은 충청 천안시 충남테크노파크 디스플레이혁신공정센터에서 충남테크노파크 디스플레이혁신공정단과 QD-LED 기술개발 및 공정 실증을 위한 업무 협약식을 가졌다.이에 따라 앞으로 모플랫은 충남테크노파크를 거점으로 QD-LED 소재 개발에 나서게 된다.자발광 소재인 QD는 수 나노미터 크기의 초미세 반도체 입자로, 전기나 빛의 자극에 특정 파장의 빛을 매우 순수한 색으로 방출하는 특성을 가지고 있다.모플랫은 이러한 퀀텀닷 기술을 활용한 실내·외 자동차 라이팅을 개발해 자동차 전장 부품 분야에서 세계 최초

items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Quantum hardware developers, software providers and supercomputing centers are adopting the community-built Slurm workloads manager and the NVIDIA quantum platform to integrate quantum processors, design future systems and develop scientific applications. November 16, 2026 by Sam Stanwyck 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Beating the Bottleneck Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments.
